substantiveWordCount.method: Main article prose and section headings; excludes main title, JSON metadata and source/applicability footer.

authorship: 100 separately authored English explanations. Shared GM monitor families retain their actual channel/sensor identity and published common diagnostic logic; no unique repairs or fitment invented to create artificial variation.
sourceReviewMeaning: checked means the cited manufacturer evidence was reviewed, not approval by a mechanic or permission to publish. needs-review records a real unresolved issue in the source; supported explanations remain useful and omitted facts are identified.
researchMethod: Read local original manufacturer PDFs and page-ordered text supplied in assignments. Inspected original page images where rotated/merged GM tables, page continuations or incomplete text could cause row misidentification. NHTSA archives are manufacturer communications, not generic dictionary descriptions.
scopeRules: GM file-level model lists were not treated as per-code fitment. Numerical limits are restricted to the cited historical controller/monitor.
NHTSA manufacturer cases preserve model, year, engine/build or market limits, module identity, failure suffix and repair-history details when supplied.
Historical software-release expectations are described as forecasts at publication, not current availability. Expired program terms are not offered as present coverage.
High-voltage, braking, steering and restraint explanations do not provide bypass, hazardous probing or disassembly instructions.
The 14 bundle-only original candidates were replaced by root-approved, globally reserved manufacturer cases; no removed bundle-only code was written.
